I am an old woman, 71 years, and this small plot near my house has my coffee and enset trees that my husband and I planted long ago. These are perennial crops, already grown — I do not need to buy seed, and I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from the cooperative, but I put the manure from my few animals and the household ash around the trees. My grandchildren help me weed and harvest, and for coffee picking time my neighbor's son comes to help for a few days in exchange for some grain.
